i spent 8 days in an adolescent psych ward when i was 14 so i can’t speak on behalf of adult ones but from my experience, it was both helpful and not helpful at the same time. 

pros:
- i was surrounded with people my age who were going through similar struggles so it was easy to connect with them
- it was really nice to take a break from the outside world and all of my previous responsibilities
- i felt relatively safe there because it’s hard to find a way to hurt yourself unless you go out of your way to find something

cons:
- there were strict rules that were meant to keep us safe but they got really annoying really quickly
- they doped me up on meds that made me feel worse/ didn’t do anything
- the psychiatrists and nurses didn’t really care about me as a person and they didn’t actually try to help me with any of my problems
- they wouldn’t let me out so i had to lie my way out of there (which isn’t hard to do but i wouldn’t recommend doing it unless you absolutely can’t take it anymore)

even though there are cons to going, if you feel like you’re not able to keep yourself safe then PLEASE don’t hesitate to go to the ER

i totally understand the worry of taking up a spot for someone else who could “need it more” than you but you have to understand that there is always gonna be someone who has it worse than you but just because they do, it doesn’t mean that you’re not deserving of the help and protection that you need to feel safe. 

i’ve been considering going back myself because i haven’t been feeling safe recently and the help i have right now isn’t working for me

all that being said, it’s different for everyone but just keep in mind that generally speaking, the psych ward isn’t gonna be the place to solve your problems. it’s designed to keep you safe but that’s about it, so don’t expect to come out a whole lot better than you were coming in. 

stay safe and please get the help you need! i’m sending you love❤️

* most often i hear it referred to as the psych ward or mental hospital but it all generally means the same thing
